faces.f: They are cautious with their body language and facial expressions. Any stray movement could betray the positions of the troops they protect and cost many lives.

"When one of us prospers, the pride prospers."
—Jazal Goldmane
"Better the dead depart utterly than be enslaved."
The sky rang with the cries of armored seraphs, and the darkness made a tactical retreat.

"As peace should be—gentle yet unstoppable."
—Augustin IV
Naya's trees grow tall and sturdy. Their foliage intertwines to form dewcups, rainwater pools where the elves gather to celebrate life.

"Purge the damned, for they have no place among the righteous!"
—Seeta of Thraben
Infinitely powerless.
Its wings disturb more than air.
"Such a lord as this—all virtues' height—Had never been, nor ever was again."
Unaware of Lorwyn's diversity, it sees only itself, reflected a thousand times over.
She incubates her eggs in gold and mana.

"A great warrior studies many different disciplines and takes the best from each."
—Gideon Jura
"Serra isn't dead. She lives on through me."
Once you've been dragged down the currents of time, you'll never quite trust your own permanence again.
The lives of elves are long, but their memories are longer. Even after death, they do not desert their homes.
Debates between wizards are never purely academic.

"Choices belong to those with the luxuries of time and distance. We have neither. I recommend we proceed with the plan to destroy all shrines of the kami."
—Lady Azami, letter to Sensei Hisoka

"The Origin Query will wait. We must ensure we survive to return to it."
—Pelyus, vedalken ordinar
Kongming and Lu Su tricked Wei troops into shooting over 100,000 arrows at them to later use against the Wei at Red Cliffs.
At Red Cliffs, Kongming and Zhou Yu each wrote his plan for defeating Wei on the palm of his hand. They laughed as they both revealed the same word, "Fire."

"Do as I think, not as I do."
—Jace Beleren

"As long as I pull the strings, you will dance."
—Tezzeret
"The specimen seems to be broken."

"There is nothing you can do that I cannot simply deny."
—Ertai, wizard adept
Sentience is its natural habitat.
The winds of change have a mind of their own.

"The union of sea and sky makes a perfect cover."
—Talrand, sky summoner
It lingers near the outposts of the Makindi Trenches, inadvertently granting another layer of defense.
"This is a sacred duty. Master Beleren's trust has bought an eternity of my loyalty."

"I'd build an entire fortress of them if I could."
—Mzali, Lighthouse archmage
"Opportunity isn't something you wait for. It's something you create."
"Long live . . . me."

"The cost of your opposition will be extracted from your wits."
—Nekusar, the Mindrazer

"True riches are found in the mazes of the mind."
—Tamiyo, the Moon Sage
Whether mechanical or biological, life finds a way to propagate itself.

"All clouds should be so organized."
—Isperia
"Plans evolved within the tent decide a victory 1,000 *li* away."
Guarding the ship is the Thornwinds' first concern. Getting along with the locals ranks fourth or fifth at best.

"Do not speak the name of the sea, for if it should hear you and rise up, no fortress in the world could hide you."
—Gimara of Halimar
"I could see in the other mage's eyes that he'd thought of it too. Then it became a race to exploit the knowledge first."

"It's not the darkness I fear but dull and numbing shades of gray."
—Sydri, galvanic genius

"The awestruck birds gazed at Wonder. Slowly, timidly, they rose into the air."
—*Scroll of Beginnings*

"Whatever Yawgmoth marks, dies. There is no escape."
—Tsabo Tavoc, Phyrexian general
Sometimes death comes knocking. Sometimes it tears down the walls.

"As with any malevolent being, the trick is knowing how long you can afford to keep it in your service."
—Liliana Vess
The demon Griselbrand dared to stand against Avacyn, earning him the loathing of thousands and the admiration of a few.
There is nothing more repulsive than a cockroach—except a cockroach and all its friends.

"Better to starve to death than be bored to death."
—Liliana Vess
What is a sliver of one's soul compared to unimaginable wealth?
Insidious fear can be the undoing of the greatest of armies.

"This is why we don't go out in banewasp weather."
—Rannon, Vithian holdout

"No matter how far we push into Stensia, undeath will always remain in these lands."
—Terhold, archmage of Drunau
Nightscape masters don't stop at raising the spirit of a fallen battlemage. They raise the flesh along with it.

"There are dark, ancient arts that fascinate even me."
—Sorin Markov
Because the dead have no will to resist.
Other Phyrexians have nightmares about the gargantua.
Death is no excuse to stop working.
As the druids had devoted their lives to preserving Dominaria, so did they devote their deaths.
"The end is justified in being mean. Or something like that."

"Blood is constant. Every drop I drink, someone must bleed."
—Vradeen, vampire nocturnus
The assassin sees only throats and hears only heartbeats.

"It's a difficult task to quarantine a plague that moves with the clouds."
—Esara, healer adept
In matters of life and death, he trusts his gut.
Even the lost and undead need a protector.
In war, the best leaders are open to all tactics.
"You wish for great destruction? It is done, my master."

"Let them cry for mercy. The only one who can hear them is me."
—Siglind the Conqueror

"Something down there has an appetite for what we're standing on. Let's hope it doesn't want seconds."
—Samila, Murasa Expeditionary House
Nothing impresses goblins more than something that's bound to kill them.
One mogg to aim the catapult, one mogg to steer the rock.
He wants to watch Ravnica burn, one soul at a time.
The magus still hears the roar of the crowds. They're gone, but the will to compete remains.

"What say you, my most trusted advisors? . . . Advisors?"
—Edra, merfolk sovereign
Disaster stalks with gaping jaws across unready lands.
Something roams the killing places, sniffing the guilt of the slayers, stalking them on iron paws.
Ever since the disaster, the city's survivors viewed the star-strewn sky with dread.
In the Skyfang Mountains, one misstep can mean the end of an entire clan.
It lives in the mountaintops, feeds at the mountains' feet, and kills anything it finds on the path between.

"You deify nature as female—kind and gentle—yet you cringe at what is natural."
—Mirri of the *Weatherlight*
The rhythm isn't a call to arms, but a signal that the goblins have made a new enemy.
"Listen to the roar! Feel the thunder! The Immersturm shouts its approval with every bolt of lightning!"

"Never subtle nor cryptic is the reckoning of the mighty."
—Mayael the Anima

"How thin is the veneer of civilization! A modest measure of panic will wash it off completely."
—Guard Erdrud of An Karras

"May your day never match your expectations."
—Scriptus Fleen, flectomancer
The accusations spread like hungry flames.
Its insatiable hunger quickly depletes a region of prey. It must migrate from place to place to feed its massive bulk.
It sees shaped stone and carved wood as mutilations.

"I have been trapped in the lizard's lair for days. It seems to regard me as its child and will not let me leave."
—Aevar Borg, northern guide, journal entry
All seeds share a common bond, calling to each other across infinity.

"Hunters feed on the fear of their prey."
—Garruk Wildspeaker
"I feel the vine-rhythm as my friends drive the beast to me. I will not miss my mark."
The spires of Ravnica are no different from the tall trees of other planes. The elves navigate and protect them just the same.
"Verdant bloom does exist. It merely hides for its own safety."
Life is eternal. A lifetime is ephemeral.

"Don't be fooled. If it were as docile as it looks, it would've died off long ago."
—Yon Basrel, Oran-Rief survivalist
"Words lie. People lie. The land tells the truth."

"We are one with the wild things. Life blooms from our fingertips and nature responds to our summons."
—Jade creed

"Give up these unnatural weapons, these scrolls. Heart and mind and fist are enough."
—Zyd, Kamahlite druid
It turns prey into predator.
When civilization encroaches on nature, Zendikar encroaches back.
Some said killing the thallids only encouraged them.
"Here lies Gond, hero of Safehold Taldwen. May he ever guide our quest."
When the forests became havens for evil, the archmages devised new ways to cleanse the wilds.

"When the land is angry, so are they."
—Nissa Revane

"All we know about the Krosan Forest we have learned from those few who made it out alive."
—Elvish refugee

"You cannot imagine what eyes you may look through tomorrow."
—Aerona, elder druid

"See, the land itself raises an altar to the ascendancy of nature."
—Mayael the Anima
Slain warriors were buried with a tree sapling, so they would become a part of the forest after death.
By the time the spider comes to slurp up its dinner, its victims have been partially dissolved by acidic silk.

"The hypocrisy of these elves is thicker than steel—destroying 'unnatural metal' with their own enchanted swords."
—Kara Vrist, Neurok agent
It's the only water source in miles of desert, but the local tribes avoid it at all costs.
Its beak rends flesh and bone, exposing the tender marrow of dream.
Those who worship the great gargantuans could hardly be expected to fight with a subtle weapon.

"Practice compassion and mercy. But know when they must end."
—Aurelia
Jund's dragons hoard only sangrite crystals. Its wurms aren't so picky.
A pretty bauble of persecution.
There is always a greater power.
Plate mail, the skin of the chest, the rib cage, the heart—all useless against the mage who can reach directly for the soul.

"There are deep, deep places in this world that have long burned hot with little regard for the whitening of the earth's thin skin."
—Sek'Kuar, Deathkeeper

"Wisdom can be summed up in two rules: Control what you can. Eliminate what you cannot."
—Dromar, the Banisher
When the rebels couldn't breach the castle to kill Lalor the Obstinate, they tried a more internal approach to depose the pretender king.
"I craved enlightenment, and Crucius's etherium opened my eyes. I would share my sight with you, but first you must believe."
Yavimaya lights the quickest path to battle.
He can stir the gentlest spirit to wild ferocity.

"So many choices. Shall I choose loathing, hate, or malice today?"
—Eliza of the Keep
"Crovax knows we're coming now," said a grinning Sisay. "I just sent the *Predator* crashing into his stronghold."
Jund pulses with raw energy, waiting for shamans to shape it into useful form.

"The best experiments are those whose successes replicate themselves."
—Yolov, Simic bioengineer
The sacred Anima's eyes are blind to all but the grandest truths.
Deep in nature's core lies a potential unsullied by greed or civilization.
His enemies wondered if the lich king's brutal death and unnatural rebirth had been his plan all along.
"The only action worth taking is one with an unknown outcome."
Naya teems with gargantuans, titanic monsters to whom both nature and civilization defer.
"Time and space are just new battlefields to be mastered."
"Take up the quill, and feel your future flow into the runes."

"Nature is the ultimate mindless destroyer, capable of power and ferocity no army can match, and the Gruul follow its example."
—Trigori, Azorius senator

"There is only one way of life in Jund: feed on the weak until you are cut down by something stronger."
—Jorshu of Clan Nel Toth
The orcs believe Sek'Kuar still lives in the Karplusan Mountains, gathering his dead army, intent on revenge.
To gain audience with the hegemon, one must bring a riddle she has not heard.
They lament the doom that is coming to Bant without realizing the part their own leaders have played in it.

"Birth and death are both reversible."
—Nicol Bolas

"Some think its immunity to countermagic evolved because of the constant mage attacks on Naya. I think it just ate a bunch of wizards."
—Broka, drumhunter
No one has properly answered her favorite riddle: "Why should I spare your life?"
The vast network of predation on Jund has actually caused some strange creatures to adapt to being eaten.
His name means "he who paints the earth red."
The scullers beneath Esper keep strixes as trained pets, and set them loose when a fare refuses to pay.

"Esper, like any work of art, can be truly appreciated only from a distance."
—Tezzeret
The nacatl called this new species "vetli," their word for poison arrows.
Moonstones grant limited foresight but unlimited advantages.

"She spoke of mystery and portent, of such unfathomable things that my mind screamed for pity."
—*The Seer's Parables*
Olka collected the evening mist for years, studying its secrets. Once she learned its essence, she could vanish with a thought.
Knowledge brings the sting of disillusionment, but the pain teaches perspective.

"Etherium is limited. Innovation is not."
—Tezzeret
The mysterious purpose of two of the rings had eluded Esper mages—until now.

"The higher the mind soars, the greater its understanding of the law."
—Isperia

"In these bloodstains I will find the fingerprints of our oppressors."
—Anowon, the Ruin Sage

"Tomorrow wears yesterday's face."
—Kordel the Cryptic
Lord Rondor arrived for battle with sixty war elephants, ten catapults, and two hundred of his finest archers. Then he saw the battlefield . . .

"It reflects the purity of Mirrodin-that-was."
—Koth of the Hammer

"It offers you what you want, not what you need."
—Braids, dementia summoner
It is a monument as austere, unyielding, and inscrutable as Esper itself.
Like most features of Grixis, the obelisks that remain from the time of Alara now exist only for dark exploitation.
Volcanic ash-winds batter it, climbing vines overwhelm it, dragonfire roasts it, and yet it still stands as a testament to a forgotten world.
The kor send their thopter kites to see if the land is in a welcoming mood.

"Tools and artisans can be destroyed, but the act of creation is inviolate."
—Elspeth Tirel
"The shadow travels toward the apex. I predict we will soon see the true measure of darkness."
The symbol of the Conclave is one of unity, with tree supporting sun and sun feeding tree.

For the Simic Combine, its sigil serves not as an emblem of honor but as a trademark. Its familiar image on any biological commodity attests to superb craftsmanship, ingenious innovation, and higher cost.
Lost to time is the artificer's art of trapping light from a distant star in a ring of purest gold.
Enlightenment is not gained by striking the bell or hearing its toll. It's found in the silence that follows.
Paradoxically, to tilt the massive jug for a sip, you'd need the energy of the giant's tonic.
Jort the Thunder-Mad spent his life perfecting a way to harness the power of the heavens.
The ur-golem etchings begin by celebrating Mirrodin's creator, a golem of almost limitless power. They end by cursing its protector, a being called Memnarch.
"This may hurt a lot."
It is the forest beyond the horizon, the mountain waiting to be climbed, the new land across the endless sea.
Some say the knowledge lost during the Ritual of Rebuking is returned through the well's waters.

"We must rely on our own knowledge, not on the dogma of the seekers or the mutterings of the sphinxes."
—Tullus of Palandius
Enter the Senate, the seat of justice and the foundation of Ravnican society.
Bant's hearts are as pure as its air and as bright as its skies.
Enter with merciful hearts. Exit with battle cries.
When defeat is near and guidance is scarce, all eyes look in one direction.

"They say the ruins of Sedraxis were once a shining capital in Vithia. Now it is a blight, a place to be avoided by the living."
—Olcot, Rider of Joffik
Enter and become a mastermind of spies, lies, and deception.
Esper is an expansive canvas painted by precise, controlling hands.
Without the interfering hands of civilization, nature will always shape itself to its own needs.
Enter those who are starving and sick. You are welcome among the Swarm when the rest of Ravnica rejects you.

"I love what they've done with the place."
—Liliana Vess
There is no height above Grixis that is free from the stench of death.
Enter and leave the shackles of society behind.

"Let your heels point you home."
—Ancient blessing
Enter those with the vision to create and the daring to release their creations.
The sky is the dragon's throne, the seat from which it issues its fiery decrees.
On Naya, ambition and treachery are scarce, hunted nearly to extinction by the awe owed to terrestrial gods.

"They're still here?! The cockroach may have finally met its match."
—Teferi
Between the thunderous footfalls of Naya's behemoths lie moments of perfect quiet.
Enter to find wealth, security, and eternal life . . . for just a small price up front.
Enter and indulge your darkest fantasies, for you may never pass this way again.
Jund is a world as cruel as those who call it home. Their brutal struggles scar the land even as it carves them in its image, a vicious circle spiraling out of control.
For wisdom's sake, it was built high to gaze on all things. For glory's sake, it was built high as a testament of power. For strength's sake, it was built high to repel all attacks.
Enter and rejoice! The Conclave stands united, open to one and all.
Enter and comprehend the perfection of orchestrated life.
Those who bring nothing to the temple take nothing away.

"Though their ideals are leagues apart, Urza's and Mishra's creations have a surprising harmony with one another."
—Tocasia, journal entry
In the autumn, she casts her seeds across the streets below, and come spring, her children rise in service to the Conclave.
She arrived like a meteorite, and the enemy fell in a shock wave of holy vengeance.
Her presence on the battlefield can transform an unruly mob into a disciplined army.
Some protection requires a bit of finesse.

"We will descend upon you like a plague of locusts to purge you from our lands!"
—Hirov, commander of the Thousand Swords

"They had it coming."
—Squire Imalia, savior of Thiswick

"As my kha, he is the source of my inspiration. As my brother, he is the embodiment of my aspirations."
—Ajani Goldmane
The militia formed up in the central plaza awaiting the onslaught, but the giants never quite made it.
These waters remain uncharted, but not for lack of trying.
What are the orders of a king or the demands of a creed next to such melodies?
Most see krakens as wantonly violent, failing to notice their meticulous attention to detail when dismantling a vessel.
"Just a taste?"
"Geralf, must you always whine? I agreed to nothing. I'll raise ghouls anytime I wish."

"Such an affliction appears to seek out the pure."
—Byro, plague doctor
It shambled from the cloud of ash and bone dust, undeterred by its own extinction.

n: Ob Nixilis of the Black Oath

faces.f:
"There are always leftovers."
—Derecht, flesh carver
"It has been my experience that disasters like to strike in pairs."
"She will come back to me."
Nothing breaks the monotony like a good old-fashioned riot.
"Where a lesser mind sees junk, I see infinite potential."
Nothing escapes its gaze—or its breath.
Its wings beat to the howls of war and fan the fires of rage.

"I saw the devastation when the juggernauts crashed the walls of An Karras. Then I got to thinking."
—Janji, sylvan druid
It claws at the earth in a vain attempt to reclaim what it once was.
Pharika has written her secrets on its bones so that only the worthy may discover them.

"Hold the line, hold the li—"
—General Srok, last words
Few who encounter the strange, human-like grove leave once the lilting chorus of the dryads reaches their ears.
If you hear it, it's too late.

"Knowledge is a stain that only instinct and ferocity can cleanse."
—Drarg, wolfcaller
It harmonizes with the essence of its master.
Every head it rests upon winds up severed.
Mages come from far and wide to bathe in its wisdom.

"The crucible yields what you have forged in your mind. You need only reach in and draw the masterwork forth."
—Wahara, Keeper of the Crucible
Its collapse is like the lashing out of a long-dead civilization that resents being forgotten.
She doesn't escort the dead to the afterlife, but instead raises them to fight and die again.

We all must profit for peace to last.
—Mercadian saying

"Trust me, your lost fingers and toes are nothing compared to the lost treasures of Sejiri."
—Zahr Gada, Halimar expedition leader
Avacyn's holy warriors kept hope alive in her darkest hours. Now they will carry that hope across Innistrad.

"No doubt the arbiters would put you away, after all the documents are signed. But I will have justice now."
—Alovnek, Boros guildmage
Its wings disturb more than air.
"Your superstitions and mumblings are useless chaff before my righteousness."
"I am not Raksha. I never will be. But I refuse to be the kha who watched her pride be torn asunder."
"Why keep such trinkets? They only add weight to your travels."
Their war forgotten, the nations of Bant stood united in the face of a common threat.
"In these halls there is no pass or fail. Your true test comes with the first full moon."
The path back to the world of the living is murky and bewildering. A geist may not even realize that it's terrifying its own loved ones.
Wars are won with strength, valor, and numbers—especially numbers.
"A richer people could give more but they could never give as much."
When angels despair, what hope can remain for mortals?
Some timelines forever fray, branch, and intermingle. Others end abruptly.
"Serra isn't dead. She lives on through me."

"Like dawn's first light, blind the unprepared and banish the shadows."
—Skyhunter creed

"The dead have it easy. They suffer no more. If breaking their rest helps the living, so be it."
—Olka, mistmeadow witch
A blazing sun that never sets.
There may exist powers even greater than Phyrexia.
Dozens of spells known only to the Auriok elders were lost, but the next generation, galvanized by war, devised even more potent magic.
After the Battle of Liet Field, the white sun crested above Taj-Nar, bringing hope to all who survived the carnage.
Saltfield nomads call a sudden storm a "whitemane."

"We draw our power from the infinite ocean of the mind, where all manner of things can be conceived."
—Azure creed
Water calls to water, and the world is left exhausted and withered in its wake.

"It's hard to say which is more satisfying: the search for that missing piece or fitting that piece into place."
—Evo Ragus
"Four parts molten bronze, yes . . . one part frozen mercury, yes, yes . . . but then what?"
"The treasure in my mind is greater than any worldly glory."
The Izzet specialize in unnatural disaster.

"There is nothing you can do that I cannot simply deny."
—Ertai, wizard adept
Gerrard savored a grim smile as the Phyrexian portals disappeared behind the *Weatherlight*.

"I don't have time for you right now."
—Teferi

"The union of sea and sky makes a perfect cover."
—Talrand, sky summoner
They only appear in emergencies, and emergencies never last long.
"Roil tide! Roil tide! Tie yourselves down!"
When Lorthos emerges from his deepwater realm, the tides bow to his will and the coastline cowers in his presence.
Some spellcrafting mistakes go on to become spells of their own.

"Limitless power is glorious until you gain limitless understanding."
—Ixidor, reality sculptor
"The secret entrance should be near."
"A riddle is nothing more than a trap for small minds, baited with the promise of understanding."
After a hundred failed experiments, Urza was stunned to find that common silver passed through the portal undamaged. He immediately designed a golem made of the metal.
"Ribbit."
His slaves crave death more than they desire freedom. He denies them both.

"May you wake to find you were only ever a dream."
—Mephidross curse

"Whatever Yawgmoth marks, dies. There is no escape."
—Tsabo Tavoc, Phyrexian general

"Under the suns, Mirrodin kneels and begs us for perfection."
—Geth, Lord of the Vault
He relishes the devotion of his Skirsdag puppets and their belief that it will earn them immortality.
His verdict is always guilty. His sentence is always death.
"Lord Bolas has shown me how each miserable little life holds untold resources."
"If our former masters would have us kneel again, they shall feel our defiance slashed across their membranes."
Those who forget the horrors of the past are doomed to re-meet them.
Crovax gazed on the dead, and for one dark moment he saw a banquet.
Death in form and function.
All that remains of the Cabal are the echoes in its deepest vault. Yet those who hear the echoes feel a power undiminished by the dust of ages.

"Let go your grudges, or risk wandering the bogs forever in a murderous rage."
—Hildin, priest of Avacyn

"It's only torture if you're strong enough to survive. Otherwise, it's a simple, gruesome death. I'm happy either way."
—Liliana Vess
In life, the nantuko study nature by revering it. In death, they study nature by disemboweling it.
His victims don't have time to feel despair.
"I have schemed too long to be supplanted by dead gods. If I cannot have this world, no one can."
Other Phyrexians have nightmares about the gargantua.
The dead know lessons the living haven't learned.
"Avacyn has deserted you. I welcome your devotion in her stead."
Little agonies pave the way to greater power.
"Thraben's pleas fall on deaf ears. Ours do not."
When tempers run high, it's easy to lose your head.
Darkness doesn't always send its minions to do its dirty work.
Linger on death's door and risk being invited in.
When the blood hunt lost its thrill, she looked for less tangible means of domination.
The priest cast Xantcha to the ground. "It is defective. We must scrap it."
Whether trained, ridden, or eaten, few goblin military innovations have rivaled the bug.

"Holy places are no longer sanctuary from death, and death is no longer sanctuary from anything."
—Thalia, Knight-Cathar
"Avacyn has abandoned us! We have nothing left except what we can take!"

"For dim-witted, thick-skulled genetic mutants, they have pretty good aim."
—Sisay, captain of the *Weatherlight*
"I wrecked your metal guy, boss. But look! I made you an ashtray."
He collects the precious metals, and then converts the rest to propellant.
Elementals are ideas given form. This one is the idea of "smashitude."

"Where will you run when I punish you with the very ground you flee on?"
—Nicol Bolas
Disaster stalks with gaping jaws across unready lands.
Ever since the disaster, the city's survivors viewed the star-strewn sky with dread.
Remade by Eldrazi magic, Tuktuk inspired an entire clan of misguided goblins.
The slag-workers wasted no time in creating their own flare pulses to cleanse the area of the *incompleat*.
"Obey!"
"The beasts of the wild are my senses. It is through their eyes that all knowledge shall come to me."
Massive, mindless, and imbued with one terrible purpose.
"The light of beauty protects our journeys through darkness."
He knows the name of every elf born in the last four centuries. More importantly, they all know his.

"Life grows everywhere. My kin merely find those places where it grows strongest."
—Nissa Revane
The spires of Ravnica are no different from the tall trees of other planes. The elves navigate and protect them just the same.
"From a tiny sprout, the greatest trees grow and flourish. May the seeds of your mind be equally fruitful."

"The more our numbers grow, the more I gain hope that Volrath and his cursed stronghold will one day fall."
—Eladamri, Lord of Leaves
The infamous Ezuri commands the highest bounty the vedalken have ever placed upon an outlaw.
"Verdant bloom does exist. It merely hides for its own safety."
A scavenger's favorite appetizer is death.

"Nothing in nature goes to waste, not even the rotting corpse of a good-for-nothing, blood-sucking vampire."
—Halana of Ulvenwald
No spot in nature is truly barren.
"Eyeblights are easy to track. Just follow the imperfections."
Elves of the immaculate class weave flora into living creatures—sometimes to endorse an elite warrior, sometimes to create a breathing work of art.
In a culture of beauty, the most beautiful are worshipped as gods.

One bone broken for every twig snapped underfoot.
—Llanowar penalty for trespassing
From the highest tiers of Dawn's Light Palace to the deepest shade of Wren's Run, the silver notes of the horn shimmer through the air, and all who hear it feel its pull.
"Beauty determines value, and we determine beauty."
Nature doesn't walk.
As the Phyrexian contagion corroded Karn's body, the praetors whispered psalms to corrupt his mind.
Titania rewards all who honor the forest by making them a living part of it.
For each creature that arrives in its audience, the sage imparts another piece of ancient wisdom for all to hear.

"When the land is angry, so are they."
—Nissa Revane
"What was once formed by masons, shaped by smiths, or given life by mages, I will return to the embrace of the earth."
By the time the spider comes to slurp up its dinner, its victims have been partially dissolved by acidic silk.
It's there when a seed sprouts, when gourds ripen on the vines, and when the reapers cut the grains under the Harvest Moon.
"Not all paths are found on the forest floor."

"He has been to the heart of the wood. Did you truly expect to wield power over him?"
—Oakhide druid
Their arrows are tipped with basilisk eyes and fletched with cockatrice feathers.
